To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the water immersion of GFRP specimens at 80°C caused weight loss due to the dissolution of unsaturated polyester resin.
the reduction in elastic moduli and bending strength of GFRP composites immersed in hot water was related to weight changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation between the weight changes and the reduction in bending strength and modulus of GFRP immersed in hot water.
the relation between the weight changes and the reduction in bending properties of GPRP panels immersed in water.
the relation between the weight changes and the reduction in bending properties of G-FRP panels due to water immersion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reduction in the elastic modulus and the strength due to water absorption was greater in the panels with higher filler contents and the reduction in the modulus was larger than the reduction in the strength.
the weight loss due matrix dissolution was more important than the weight gain due water absorption in terms of the bending properties.
there is no clear relationship between the weight gain due water absorption and the strength and elastic modulus reduction of the GFRP panels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
weight loss was more dominant in the case of panels with higher filler content.
there is a good relation between weight changes of the GFRP panels and the bending properties.
the weight loss is a better indicator for the reduction in elastic properties than the weight gain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction in elastic properties is due to the weight changes, and that the reduction is larger in the case of weight gain.
the weight loss of GFRP due to matrix dissolution is more significant than the weight gain due water absorption.
there is no significant relation between weight changes of the GFRP panels and the bending properties.
